messages.author: Pedro Simoes
messages.message:
Ainda recentemente vendi uma analise que só foi feita porque com AI dava para fazer com menos pessoas.

Outros clientes pagariam 2 semanas de trabalho. Este nao pagaria 2 semanas, mas pagava uma.

Pode ser interpretado tanto como “vender algo a metade do preço” como “vender algo adicional”.

Neste caso foi claramente o segundo caso.

🔗 Yung Geeski | Viral Money Charts 📊 no Instagram: "Everyone says “just buy the S&P 500.”

But since May 2005, the most concentrated version absolutely crushed it:

S&P 1: +2,651%
S&P 3: +1,599%
S&P 5: +1,589%
S&P 10: +1,213%
S&P 100: +860%
S&P 50: +845%
S&P ~3500: +824%
S&P 500: +823%

Important: “S&P 1” does NOT mean buying today’s biggest company and pretending you knew the future.

The synthetic S&P 1/3/5/10 portfolios use the largest S&P 500 companies at each historical year-end, market-cap weighted and reconstituted annually. So as market leadership changed from Exxon and Microsoft to Apple, Nvidia, etc., the portfolio changed too.

Over this period, diversification protected you from individual-company risk.

It also diversified you away from the biggest winners.

Would you actually put your money in the S&P 1 instead of the S&P 500?

Follow @yunggeeski_ for more investing data nobody bothers to chart.

Sources: Yahoo Finance; historical S&P 500 market-cap rankings via Finhacker; Invesco XLG; iShares
